0.long_answer: Blue cone monochromacy results from defects in the opsin gene array on the X‐chromosome, specifically involving the two homologous cone opsin genes that normally encode the long (L) and medium (M) wavelength-sensitive opsins. Although these genes are highly homologous, detailed molecular analyses have identified a set number of fixed nucleotide differences between them. Studies have shown that there are 19 dismorphic (i.e. non‐identical) sites between these homologous genes. This number reflects the precise count of nucleotide positions that differ between the two sequences and is important for understanding both spectral differences and the basis for the clinical phenotype observed when one of these genes is disrupted.
